headline: SSC results: Pass rate falls to 62.25%, 690,608 students fail
summary: Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon says marks reflected actual performance, while 312 institutions record zero pass rates.
details: The overall pass rate for the SSC and equivalent examinations has dropped to 62.25 percent, a decrease of 6.20 percentage points from last year's 68.45 percent.
A total of 690,608 students failed the exams, while 116,676 students achieved GPA-5.
Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon defended the decline, stating that students were awarded marks based on their actual performance and that marks cannot be awarded freely.
The number of institutions with zero pass rates has jumped to 312, prompting the government to take measures to improve their performance.
The minister also announced a change to the re-scrutiny process, where students applying for review will now have their entire answer scripts re-examined.
Next year's SSC examinations are scheduled to begin on January 7, with the goal of gradually bringing the examination calendar forward.
Other key findings show that girls outperformed boys in both the pass rate and GPA-5 achievements, and the Dhaka board topped the results.
caption:
The SSC pass rate has plummeted to 62.25%, with over 690,000 students failing.

The overall pass rate for the SSC and equivalent examinations has dropped to 62.25 percent, a decrease of 6.20 percentage points from last year's 68.45 percent.

A total of 690,608 students failed the exams, while 116,676 students achieved GPA-5.

Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon defended the decline, stating that students were awarded marks based on their actual performance and that marks cannot be awarded freely.

The number of institutions with zero pass rates has jumped to 312, prompting the government to take measures to improve their performance.

The minister also announced a change to the re-scrutiny process, where students applying for review will now have their entire answer scripts re-examined.

Next year's SSC examinations are scheduled to begin on January 7, with the goal of gradually bringing the examination calendar forward.

Other key findings show that girls outperformed boys in both the pass rate and GPA-5 achievements, and the Dhaka board topped the results.

headline: 16 Bangladeshis killed in Saudi factory fire
summary: The devastating blaze broke out at a sofa factory in Riyadh's Musa Industrial Area, claiming the lives of 16 workers on the spot.
details: At least 16 Bangladeshi nationals were killed in a devastating fire at a sofa factory in Saudi Arabia, according to the Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Ministry.
The incident occurred around 2:00 pm yesterday in the Musa Industrial Area under the Al-Shifa police station in Riyadh, with all victims dying on the spot.
Of the deceased, 13 were from Naogaon, two were from Natore, and one was from Rajshahi.
The Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh has expressed deep sorrow and is working closely with Saudi authorities to identify all the victims.
Officials from the embassy's Labour Welfare Wing are present at the site to coordinate rescue and identification efforts.
Expatriates' Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury and other government officials have expressed their condolences over the tragic loss of the lives.
caption:
16 Bangladeshi workers killed on the spot in a sofa factory fire in Saudi Arabia.

At least 16 Bangladeshi nationals were killed in a devastating fire at a sofa factory in Saudi Arabia, according to the Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Ministry.

The incident occurred around 2:00 pm yesterday in the Musa Industrial Area under the Al-Shifa police station in Riyadh, with all victims dying on the spot.

Of the deceased, 13 were from Naogaon, two were from Natore, and one was from Rajshahi.

The Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh has expressed deep sorrow and is working closely with Saudi authorities to identify all the victims.

Officials from the embassy's Labour Welfare Wing are present at the site to coordinate rescue and identification efforts.

Expatriates' Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury and other government officials have expressed their condolences over the tragic loss of the lives.
